text:
maria-support: FYI customer acme reports intermittent NXDOMAIN for their service endpoint api.acme.prod.internal.redwood.example. Started ~2026-03-16T09:10Z after a peering change. They see it from some subnets but not others.
acme-cust: yes, hitting this from our prod app tasks in subnet private-subnet-2. Other subnets in same VPC OK. Impact: 30% errors for calls to internal API, higher latency when it falls back.
tim-eng: can you paste a dig + short traceroute from one failing host and a successful host? Also which resolver configuration are you using (VPC resolver vs forwarder)?
acme-cust: failing host dig:

; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.acme.prod.internal.redwood.example @172.31.0.2 +short

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345

successful host dig:

; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.acme.prod.internal.redwood.example @172.31.0.2 +short
10.10.12.55

maria-support: interesting — same resolver but different results depending on subnet. Could be a per-subnet route53 private hosted zone association or a conditional forwarder (Route53 Resolver) returning different answers.
jamie-ops: I queried account-level hosted zones across accounts — found a private hosted zone named acme.prod.internal in a partner account (acct-999999) that overlaps the customer's zone name. That partner zone is associated to the peered VPC. If both zones exist the resolver behavior depends on which association the VPC sees first.
sofia-sre: can you share the output of `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters` and `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname acme.prod.internal` from the customer's account and the partner account? Also check VPC->HostedZone associations: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZXXXXXXXX`.
acme-cust: attaching outputs (redacted):

- Customer account hosted zone Z-CUST: acme.prod.internal (associated to VPCs: private-subnet-1, private-subnet-3)
- Partner account hosted zone Z-PART: acme.prod.internal (associated to VPCs: private-subnet-2)

route53resolver rules:
- rule R-1 forwards acme.prod.internal -> 10.2.3.4 (partner resolver endpoint) priority 10
- rule R-default system

maria-support: aha — so the partner's hosted zone is associated only to the subnet range that fails. That will cause queries from that VPC/subnet to resolve against the partner hosted zone, which likely has no records for api.acme.prod.internal and returns NXDOMAIN. That lines up with the inconsistent NXDOMAINs.
jamie-ops: :thinking: another gotcha — if there are resolver rules forwarding to the partner resolver, and that resolver sees the partner private hosted zone, it will answer authoritatively. The difference in behavior between subnets suggests the partner zone association is scoped to specific VPC/subnet. Also check if any conditional forwarders are attached to VPC resolver endpoints in only some AZs.
dns-bot: automatic-check: duplicate_private_hosted_zone_detected: name=acme.prod.internal, zones=[Z-CUST(account-1234), Z-PART(account-9999)], vpc_associations_mismatch=true
sofia-sre: recommended mitigation path:
- temporarily disassociate the partner's hosted zone from the customer's VPC (or remove the peering-based association) so only the customer's private hosted zone answers.
- if that isn't possible, change the resolver rule priority so queries for acme.prod.internal prefer the customer's authoritative resolver (or remove the forwarder rule to partner resolver).
- verify no overlapping split-horizon public->private name mapping exists.

tim-eng: quick command customers can run (customer account):

aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dnsname acme.prod.internal
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z-CUST
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z-PART --profile partner
aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=acme-vpc

jamie-ops: we coordinated w/partner account owner — they disassociated their private hosted zone from the peered VPC at 2026-03-16T09:25Z.
acme-cust: we see the error rate drop immediately, DIG now returns the expected private IP from all subnets. Confirmed by our smoke tests. :white_check_mark:
maria-support: closing loop with customer, recommended long-term: avoid overlapping private hosted zone names across peered/shared VPCs, use conditional forwarders + resolver rule priorities or centralize resolution in a shared resolver with explicit records. Also document that VPC-level associations can make resolution differ by subnet/VPC.
sofia-sre: logging action item — add a checklist for support playbook: duplicate private hosted zone check + resolver-rule priority check for split-horizon DNS tickets.
acme-cust: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround!
